title: Reviewing Income Computation Method and Considering Caregiving Expenses for Childcare Subsidy Eligibility
what_it_is: Reviewing Income Computation Method and Considering Caregiving Expenses for Childcare Subsidy Eligibility

sections.label: Childcare subsidy income means testing
sections.summary: The Ministry was asked to review income computation and caregiving expenses for childcare subsidy eligibility, and it explains per capita means testing for larger families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether the Ministry will consider (i) reviewing the computational method for the gross monthly household income and per capita income to exclude the income of other family members for young parents residing in their parents’ or relatives’ properties and (ii) factoring caregiving expenses for elderly dependents into the eligibility assessments of the applicants of Additional Subsidy for childcare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: This approach looks only at the income of both parents of a child in the family and does not include the income of other family members in the household.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: However, we do allow for larger families with five or more household members to be means tested on a per capita basis, which may qualify them for higher subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Their per capita income would be computed using the income of all the family members in the household, divided by the total number of family members in the household.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: And such families would receive the more favourable means tested result of the two processes.

sections.label: Feedback on means testing processes
sections.summary: The Ministry says it stays close to the ground, hears feedback on whether means testing processes are streamlined and effective, and will make necessary changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Generally, it pertains to feedback and making sure that we stay close to the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: We do hear from them in terms of the feedback, whether the means testing processes are streamlined, effective and really serve our residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: We will not shy away from making necessary changes when we do get some feedback.
